correctness.rationale: For a regular value w, partial fractions identify the z^{-1} coefficient at infinity of s(z)/(P(z)−w) with the sum of s(ζ)/P′(ζ) over the fiber; the polynomial part contributes nothing. Expanding in w, the term of index j is s(z)/P(z)^{j+1} times w^j. With deg s≤d(m+1)−2, all j≥m are O(z^{-2}); the trace is polynomial of degree <m, identically zero for m=0. The real Jacobian |P′|² leaves precisely this trace when testing against P′ Q_m^E(P)/d. Critical values are a finite null set, and the area formula is valid for Borel targets without boundary hypotheses. It also gives d regular preimages a.e. and the squared norm factor d/d²; boundedness and positive area follow from properness and that same area formula. Positive definiteness proves uniqueness. For the disk the monomial w^{k−1} has squared norm πR^{2k}/k in dx dy, hence the unique monic derivative divided by n=dk is P′P^{k−1}/d. Integration gives exactly P^k+c and the squared derivative minimum πnR^{2k}. The exterior Green function gives cap=R^{1/d}, including disconnected or critical-level lemniscates. The proof includes degree one and m=0 (vacuous testing if the Bergman degree is zero). Inspected but did not run verify.py; an independent check via direct rational simple-fiber sums and reciprocal Taylor coefficients (python3 reproductions/frozen_math_checks.py, pullback) passed 60 finite comparisons, which do not establish the universal result.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The capacity upper bound on an infimum cannot alone show that the exhibited derivative reaches that infimum. Exact orthogonality is what supplies this missing direction. Credit the existing implications where their hypotheses apply, not an extension to all targets.
